title: Predictive soft-reserve buffering, temporary boost accounting, and overrun invoicing policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Introduce a predictive soft-reserve buffer and a debt-accounting window for temporary boosts on Dedicated capacity. The goal is to give customers predictable throughput guarantees while offering controlled temporary boosts with transparent amortized billing. This ticket defines the runtime accounting, API config surface, operator controls, telemetry, and rollout plan for an adaptive soft-reserve + smoothing invoicing model.

Background & motivation:
Customers on Dedicated want two competing things: (1) predictable throughput and latency guarantees for steady-state traffic, and (2) the ability to handle short lived spikes without lengthy procurement cycles. Current burst handling either entirely relies on isolated surge pools (hard limits and sudden overage charges) or opaque invoice adjustments which cause support load. We need a middle ground that: (a) provides measurable short-term headroom, (b) caps instantaneous risk per-customer, and (c) smooths billing so occasional spikes don't trigger surprising one-off overage invoices.

Goals / success criteria:
- Define a "soft-reserve buffer" (SRB) concept: a small, priced pool that can be consumed instantly and replenished.
- Implement predictive allocation logic that uses recent usage momentum to recommend SRB sizes per customer.
- Introduce a debt-accounting window (configurable, default 24h) that records net boost consumption and amortizes charges across the billing period using pro-rata smoothing.
- Expose admin and customer controls for max boost, burn-rate limits, and forced reclaim thresholds.
- Provide clear telemetry and invoice line items showing baseline usage, boost consumption, amortized boost charge, and unapplied debt.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does NOT implement marketplace-based surge-pools or auctioning across tenants.
- It does not change long-term reserved capacity SLAs; SRB is explicitly transient and subject to reclaim.

Proposal (runtime + accounting):
1) Soft-reserve buffer (SRB): each Dedicated tenant may be assigned an SRB size (units: boost-credits equivalent to throughput slots). SRB can be set by customer or suggested by our predictive service. SRB consumption is recorded as "boost_units_used" in the request path.
2) Predictive suggestion engine: a short-running forecasting job (window: 15m to 2h) computes recommended SRB based on p90 traffic slope, scheduled events (customer-provided), and historical burst patterns. Recommendations surfaced in Console and via API.
3) Debt-accounting window: when SRB is exhausted, temporary boosts can still be granted up to a configurable soft cap (percent of baseline capacity). Any consumption beyond SRB enters a "debt bucket" with timestamped entries. The debt window is the period where we track and later amortize usage into billing. Default window: 24 hours.
4) Smoothing & amortized billing: At invoice generation, boost debt within the window is pro-rated onto recent invoices (or shown as a separate amortized line) instead of immediately billing the full overage charge. Customers can opt-out for immediate billing.
5) Guardrails: a per-tenant instantaneous burn-rate limiter, a cumulative debt ceiling (hard cap), and auto-throttle rules that progressively shed non-critical routes if debt approaches reclaim thresholds.
6) Fallbacks: On reclaim trigger, requests are routed to fallback model variants (lower-cost quantized variant) where applicable, and a subset of requests are rejected with 429 when SLAs must be preserved.

API / config surface (proposal):
- dedicated.srb.size: integer (boost-units) or "auto" (use recommendation)
- dedicated.srb.max_boost_pct: float (max allowed temporary boost as percent of baseline)
- dedicated.srb.debt_window_hours: integer (default 24)
- dedicated.srb.billing_mode: ["amortized", "immediate"]
- dedicated.srb.burn_rate_limit: requests/sec-per-slot
- dedicated.srb.reclaim_policy: ["soft-notify", "auto-throttle", "force-reclaim"]
These keys are surfaced in Console, via the management API, and in the Private/VPC config bundle.

Telemetry & observability:
Emit the following as first-class metrics and traces:
- dedicated.srb.recommendation (int)
- dedicated.srb.allocated (int)
- dedicated.srb.used (int / sec)
- dedicated.srb.debt_current (int)
- dedicated.srb.debt_window_events (count)
- dedicated.srb.reclaim_actions (enum events)
- dedicated.srb.billing_smoothing_applied (boolean)
Add logs for sequence of reclaim decisions and per-request annotation when a boost was used. Dashboards: per-tenant SRB utilization, debt trend, and incident table for auto-throttle events.

Billing implications & invoice design:
- Line items: baseline usage, amortized boost charge (split across invoice period), unapplied debt (if outside current invoice due to window), and support credits if any.
- Overage protection: customers can configure a monthly shield (budget cap) which will stop boost granting and trigger graceful degradation rather than generate debt beyond the cap.
- Admin reconciliation tool for finance to query boost debt timelines, apply manual credits, or adjust amortization windows for special cases.

Operational runbook & safety:
- Reclaim flow: notify customer -> auto-throttle non-critical routes -> degrade to lower-cost variant -> reject when critical.
- Alerting: trigger on rentention_exceeded (debt > 80% of ceiling), sudden +50% spike in boost usage vs. forecast, and any 5xx spike correlated with auto-throttle.
- Incident response: a postmortem template, and a PRD describing how to rollback smoothing to immediate-billing if a major finance discrepancy emerges.

Migration & rollout plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha): implement accounting and metrics, enable for internal tenants only; no billing changes.
Phase 2 (beta opt-in): expose amortized billing as opt-in for customers; Console shows recommendations and simulation of amortized invoice impact.
Phase 3 (general availability): default to amortized for new tenants; existing tenants must opt-in or approve. Finance sign-off required before GA.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Window length tradeoff: longer windows reduce invoice surprise but increase financial exposure. Propose default 24h but allow enterprise override.
- Predictive engine complexity vs. benefit: start with momentum-based heuristic before investing in ML models.
- Accounting complexity: amortization across billing cycles vs. single invoice adjustment; recommend amortization for customer experience but ensure finance has audit trail.

Next steps:
- Design review (this ticket) -> schema and metrics PR -> runtime implementation (srb allocator + debt ledger) -> Console UX -> billing integration -> opt-in beta.
